name: Handvo
subtitle: savoury fermented rice and lentil cake with a crisp sesame crust

ingredients.note: squeeze out and reserve the juice
added at the last second, for lift
most of it goes on top
use compounded-free hing to keep this gluten-free

prepNotes: Soak the rice, all three dals and the fenugreek together in plenty of water for 5 hours, then drain and grind coarse — handvo wants grit, not a smooth idli batter.
The ground batter needs 8-10 hours of fermentation, overnight in a warm spot. It should rise slightly and smell pleasantly sour.
Grate the bottle gourd only when you are ready to mix, and fold it in just before cooking; it weeps and thins the batter if it sits.

steps.text: Grind the soaked, drained rice and dals with the yogurt to a coarse batter, thick enough to drop off the spoon in a lump.
steps.tip: Add the reserved bottle gourd juice rather than water if you need to loosen it.

steps.text: Cover and leave in a warm place 8-10 hours to ferment.
Fold in the grated bottle gourd, ginger, chilli, turmeric, chilli powder, sugar, salt and coriander.
Heat 3 tbsp oil in a heavy 22cm pan, crackle the mustard and cumin seeds, then add the curry leaves, dried chilli and asafoetida.
Stir most of this tempering into the batter, leaving a spoonful and its oil in the pan.
Beat in the eno, pour the batter into the pan, level it and scatter the remaining sesame over the top.
steps.tip: Once the eno goes in the batter must hit the pan within a minute or the lift is lost.

steps.text: Cover and cook on the lowest heat 25 minutes, until the top is set and a skewer comes out clean.
steps.tip: Low and slow. On high heat you get a burnt base over raw batter.

steps.text: Drizzle the remaining oil around the edge, flip the cake or slide it under a hot grill, and cook 10 minutes more until the crust is deep brown and crisp.
Rest 10 minutes in the pan before cutting into squares.
steps.tip: Cutting hot handvo tears it; the crumb needs to firm up.

storage: Keeps 3 days refrigerated. Reheat slices in a dry pan or a 180C oven for 8 minutes to bring the crust back; the microwave makes it soggy.
